children: Profound Medical announced that five abstracts at the 15th Interventional MRI Symposium reinforce TULSA’s real-world performance, clinical differentiation and platform expansion potential.
Mayo Clinic Florida: 58 patients up to 4.5 years, 100% pad-free continence and 87.5% preserved erections for penetration beyond 12 months.
Mayo Clinic Rochester: 41 patients showed sustained PSA decline (~62%–66% at one year) with 22% biopsy-confirmed recurrence.
CARE Registry (197 patients): PSA nadirs vary by treatment extent; whole-gland median nadir 0.23 ng/mL, focal 1.10 ng/mL; catheter days shorter with less extensive treatment.
CAPTAIN randomized trial: whole-gland TULSA had >2x likelihood of preserving erectile function and pad-free continence vs. robotic prostatectomy at six months (risk ratio 2.1; p=0.004).
Technical validation: TULSA feasible on Siemens 0.55T Free.Max with improved 3D thermometry, ~1.0 ± 0.9 mm targeting accuracy and ±1.1°C baseline uncertainty.
